Southwest (Texas, Oklahoma, Kansas).text: In Texas, daytime highs ranged from the low 40s to mid-80s, while nighttime temperatures fluctuated between the 30s and 50s. A widespread rain event delivered trace amounts to nearly two inches of moisture across the region. Patchy fog, rainfall, and high humidity shortened daily harvest windows; however, harvest progress advanced to nearly 75 percent complete despite intermittent fieldwork interruptions, according to local sources. Saturated conditions occasionally delayed module transportation, but most ginning operations continued uninterrupted. In Kansas, daytime temperatures ranged from the mid-40s to mid-60s, while nighttime lows fluctuated between the 30s and 50s. Several locations in western and central Kansas received less than one-half inch of moisture, further delaying fieldwork. Defoliation remained challenging, and producers evaluated management strategies to address the issues. Some applied a second defoliant treatment, while others awaited a hard freeze to encourage leaf drop. Despite defoliation challenges, harvest progress approached 60 percent complete in some areas, less in others. Bolls remained exposed to variable weather conditions after remaining open for an extended period. All gins were operating, and some locations waited for modules to accumulate. In Oklahoma, a chilly cold front brought one-quarter to nearly two inches of widespread moisture to cotton-growing counties. Harvest progress remained slow but surpassed the halfway mark. Daytime temperatures ranged from the mid-40s to mid-60s, while overnight lows remained in the 40s. Overcast skies and humid conditions persisted throughout the reporting period. Local reports indicated defoliation remained challenging, and leaves were slow to drop from plants. Smaller-than-normal bolls with light seed development in the locks were noted. Yields varied widely. Around 60 percent has been harvested. As soils firmed, modules were slowly transported to area gins; however, not all gins were operating.

Desert Southwest (DSW).text: Spot cotton trading was inactive. Supplies and producer offerings were light. Demand was light. No forward contracting was reported during the period. Average local spot prices were higher. Foreign mill inquiries were light. Sunshine and partly cloudy conditions were observed in the DSW, with occasional light showers popping up across the region throughout the period. Daytime temperatures ranged from the 60s to the 70s with nighttime lows in the 40s to 50s. Sporadic rainfall produced moisture accumulations measuring from trace amounts up to one-quarter of an inch. Harvest continued in Arizona. Gins worked through modules staged on gin yards. The recent pattern of wet weather has slowed harvest progression in El Paso, TX, making harvest difficult for some producers. Producers continue to work around rainfall, some harvested early to avoid rain, and others are waiting for a period of dry and open conditions to harvest, according to local sources. Gins in the region expect to run until mid-December. Industry participants from across the cotton belt attended the Cotton USA Summit in Scottsdale, AZ this week on November 16-18, 2026.
